title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: An undergraduate survey of rhetorical theory organized around speech, representation, and power, moving from Greek 'origins' through symbols, signs, argument, narrative, and visual rhetoric to Latine, settler-colonial, secrecy, and digital rhetorics. Each chapter has audio or video and suggested writing assignments.
notes: Built for a 3000-level lecture course at the University of Minnesota. Download options (EPUB, PDF, XML) are on the landing page. Instructor slides and quiz banks available on request. Copyright 2022 per book page.

title: Chapter 1: What is Rhetorical Theory?
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Defines rhetorical theory, introduces the artistic proofs and rhetorical genres, and sketches several histories of the field.

title: Chapter 2: The "Origins" of Rhetorical Theory
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Asks why rhetoric's history is usually told as starting in ancient Greece, then treats sophistic knowledge and the encomium as a genre.
notes: Pairs with the book's Short Paper 1 (encomium) assignment and with Gorgias/Isocrates primary texts.

title: Chapter 3: Propaganda and the Common Good
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Traces the history of propaganda and asks how rhetoric relates to ideas of the common good.

title: Chapter 4: Rhetoric and the Freedom of Expression
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Explains why societies value free discourse, outlines First Amendment basics, and looks at exclusion, advocacy, and resistance.

title: Chapter 5: The Rhetorical Situation
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Defines the rhetorical situation, walks through an analysis of one, and introduces rhetorical ecologies as an alternative model.

title: Chapter 10: Counterpublics
authors: Flores, Carlos A.; Jones, Sarah E.
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Defines publics and counterpublics and works through case studies of counterpublic rhetoric.

title: Chapter 11: Rhetoric and Narrative
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Covers form, genre, and frame theory, Fisher's narrative paradigm, and the problem of speaking for others.

title: Chapter 12: Visual Rhetoric
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Introduces visual culture, genres of visual rhetoric, and the relation between images and power.

title: Chapter 15: Latine Rhetorical Theory
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Explains why the history of rhetorical studies matters for Latine rhetoric, how communication scholars have studied Latine rhetoric, and the key concepts, methods, and theorists of Latine rhetorical theory.
notes: One of the few openly licensed textbook chapters on Latinx/Latine rhetorics.

title: Chapter 16: Settler-Colonial Rhetoric(s)
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Defines the 'settler situation' as a counterpart to the rhetorical situation and distinguishes post-, de-, anti-, and settler-colonial frameworks.

title: Chapter 18: Digital Rhetoric(s)
parent_title: Reading Rhetorical Theory: Speech, Representation, and Power
summary: Defines digital rhetoric, offers keywords for the 'digital situation,' and discusses algorithmic bias and digital dystopia.

title: Exploring Public Speaking: Edition 4.2
authors: Tucker, Barbara; Barton, Kristin; Burger, Amy; Drye, Jerry; Hunsicker, Cathy; Mendes, Amy; LeHew, Matthew
publisher_platform: Galileo Open Learning Materials (Affordable Learning Georgia)
summary: A full introductory public speaking textbook from Dalton State College covering speech anxiety, audience analysis, research, organization, delivery, and informative and persuasive speaking.
notes: Galileo record lists Summer 2019 for Edition 4.2 and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Some catalog records (OER Commons, Touro) list CC BY; follow the authors' own CC BY-NC-SA statement. A Pressbooks copy labeled Edition 4.2 (2023) is hosted at pressbooks.ccconline.org/ppsccom1150publicspeaking/.

title: Stand Up, Speak Out: The Practice and Ethics of Public Speaking (3e)
authors: Wrench, Jason; Goding, Anne; Johnson, Danette Ifert; Attias, Bernardo Alexander
summary: A widely adopted introductory public speaking text that pairs speech-making skills with sustained attention to communication ethics, from audience analysis and research through informative, persuasive, and entertaining speeches.
notes: The University of Minnesota edition (open.lib.umn.edu/publicspeaking, 2016, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, author removed at original publisher's request) has been withdrawn from the UMN collection; its page points users to the Saylor and LibreTexts versions. Use the LibreTexts 3e (author-attributed) version.

title: Chapter 2: Ethics Matters: Understanding the Ethics of Public Speaking
authors: Wrench, Jason; Goding, Anne; Johnson, Danette Ifert; Attias, Bernardo Alexander
parent_title: Stand Up, Speak Out: The Practice and Ethics of Public Speaking (3e)
summary: Introduces ethical principles for public speakers, including honesty, respect for audiences, and responsible use of sources.

title: Chapter 4: The Importance of Listening
authors: Wrench, Jason; Goding, Anne; Johnson, Danette Ifert; Attias, Bernardo Alexander
parent_title: Stand Up, Speak Out: The Practice and Ethics of Public Speaking (3e)
summary: Distinguishes hearing from listening and offers strategies for more active and critical listening to speeches.

title: Chapter 5: Audience Analysis
authors: Wrench, Jason; Goding, Anne; Johnson, Danette Ifert; Attias, Bernardo Alexander
parent_title: Stand Up, Speak Out: The Practice and Ethics of Public Speaking (3e)
summary: Shows how to gather and use demographic and psychographic information about an audience when planning a speech.

title: Chapter 17: Persuasive Speaking
authors: Wrench, Jason; Goding, Anne; Johnson, Danette Ifert; Attias, Bernardo Alexander
parent_title: Stand Up, Speak Out: The Practice and Ethics of Public Speaking (3e)
summary: Covers theories of persuasion and practical patterns for organizing persuasive speeches.

title: Public Speaking (The Public Speaking Project)
summary: An 18-chapter introductory public speaking text that opens with the origins of public speaking and ethics and runs through critical thinking, organization, language, delivery, and speaking to a global audience.
notes: No-derivatives license: link or reproduce unchanged only. Author names taken from the LibreTexts page; confirm against the book's front matter.

title: Chapter 2: Origins of Public Speaking
parent_title: Public Speaking (The Public Speaking Project)
summary: A short history of public speaking and rhetoric for introductory speech students.
notes: No-derivatives license.

title: Chapter 14: Speaking to a Global Audience
parent_title: Public Speaking (The Public Speaking Project)
summary: Addresses speaking across cultures and languages, including audience expectations and intercultural sensitivity.
notes: No-derivatives license.

title: Advanced Public Speaking
summary: A text for second-level speech courses on writing and presenting speeches, presentation aids, speech types, and other considerations for experienced speakers.
notes: LibreTexts page last modified 2022; original publication year not stated there.

title: This Ain't Another Statement! This is a DEMAND for Black Linguistic Justice!
authors: Baker-Bell, April; Williams-Farrier, Bonnie J.; Jackson, Davena; Johnson, Lamar; Kynard, Carmen; McMurtry, Teaira
parent_title: CCCC Position Statements
publisher_platform: Conference on College Composition and Communication (NCTE)
license: All rights reserved (free access); statement says it may be printed, copied, and disseminated without permission from NCTE
topics: students' right to their own language
summary: A July 2020 CCCC statement written in response to anti-Black racism that demands teachers and researchers stop treating 'standard' academic English as the norm, stop teaching Black students to code-switch, and center Black Language in curricula and research.
notes: Authored by the 2020 CCCC Special Committee on Composing a CCCC Statement on Anti-Black Racism and Black Linguistic Justice (April Baker-Bell, chair). NCTE site footer reserves rights, but the statement text grants permission to print, copy, and disseminate. Link rather than remix.

title: Students' Right to Their Own Language
authors: Conference on College Composition and Communication
parent_title: CCCC Position Statements
publisher_platform: Conference on College Composition and Communication (NCTE)
topics: students' right to their own language
summary: The 1974 CCCC resolution affirming students' right to the dialects and language varieties in which they find their identity, with a later annotated bibliography.
notes: History on page: adopted April 1974; reaffirmed November 2003; annotated bibliography added August 2006; reaffirmed November 2014. NCTE site footer: all rights reserved. Free to read; link only.

title: Beyond Representation: Spatial, Temporal and Embodied Trans/Formations of Asian/Asian American Rhetoric
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: Introduction to enculturation's special issue on Asian/American rhetoric, moving the field beyond questions of representation toward space, time, and embodiment.
notes: Issue 27 table of contents carries enculturation's CC BY-NC-SA statement. Summary based on title and issue framing. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: In the Present and Importantly Present: Enacting a Temporal Turn for Asian American Rhetoric
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: Calls for a temporal turn in the study of Asian American rhetoric.
notes: Issue 27. Summary based on title. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: Rendering Everyday Life: Tactical Artwork by Incarcerated Japanese American Artists
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: Reads artwork made by Japanese Americans in World War II incarceration camps as tactical rhetoric of everyday life.
notes: Issue 27. Pairs with Executive Order 9066 in this corpus. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: Asian American "Hipster" Rhetoric: The Digital Media Rhetoric of the Fung Brothers
authors: Cheung, Alison Yeh; Ono, Kent A.
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: Analyzes the YouTube comedy duo the Fung Brothers as Asian American 'hipster' digital media rhetoric.
notes: Issue 27. Accessible pop-culture topic for FYC. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: Sounding Asian/America: Asian/American Sonic Rhetorics, Multimodal Orientalism, and Digital Composition
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: Examines how sound is used to mark 'Asianness' in media (multimodal Orientalism) and what that means for digital composition teaching.
notes: Issue 27. Relevant to audio/podcast assignments. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: #FuckCommunism: Embodied Rhetoric and Vietnamese Transnational Digital Practices
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: Studies embodied rhetoric in Vietnamese transnational digital practices organized around an anti-communist hashtag.
notes: Issue 27. Profanity in title; preview before assigning to first-year students. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: The Exiled Speak Back: Citizenship and Belonging in the White House 'What's Your Story?' Video Challenge
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: Analyzes how 'exiled' speakers used the White House 'What's Your Story?' video challenge to make claims about citizenship and belonging.
notes: Issue 27. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: Afterword: Disciplinary (Trans)formations: Queering and Trans-ing Asian American Rhetorics
parent_title: enculturation, no. 27 (Asian/American Rhetorical Trans/formations)
summary: An afterword calling for queer and trans approaches within Asian American rhetorics.
notes: Issue 27. Issue 27 articles dated December 18, 2018.

title: Speak Out, Call In: Public Speaking as Advocacy, 2nd ed.
summary: A public speaking textbook that treats speaking as advocacy, drawing on rhetoric, critical/cultural studies, and performance; chapters run from centering audiences and building arguments through delivery, online speaking, and ceremonial speaking.
notes: Copyright 2024 by Meggie Mapes per book page. Parts of the text are adapted from Exploring Public Speaking (Tucker and Barton, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). A first edition (2019) and a LibreTexts copy also exist. Winner of the NCA Basic Course Division 2021 Textbook of Distinction award (per secondary listing).

title: 1. Public Speaking As Advocacy
parent_title: Speak Out, Call In: Public Speaking as Advocacy, 2nd ed.
summary: Frames public speaking as purposeful, political advocacy rather than neutral information-sharing.

title: 2. Centering Audiences
parent_title: Speak Out, Call In: Public Speaking as Advocacy, 2nd ed.
summary: Shows speakers how to analyze and adapt to audiences while treating them as partners in advocacy.

title: 13. Persuasive Speaking
parent_title: Speak Out, Call In: Public Speaking as Advocacy, 2nd ed.
summary: Covers the goals, structures, and appeals of persuasive speeches.

title: Our Story Begins Here: Constellating Cultural Rhetorics
authors: Powell, Malea; Levy, Daisy; Riley-Mukavetz, Andrea; Brooks-Gillies, Marilee; Novotny, Maria; Fisch-Ferguson, Jennifer
parent_title: enculturation: a journal of rhetoric, writing, and culture, no. 18
summary: The field-defining piece by the Cultural Rhetorics Theory Lab, written as a staged performance in 'acts,' that lays out cultural rhetorics as a relational, decolonial orientation built on story, constellation, and practice.
notes: Published October 25, 2014; credited to The Cultural Rhetorics Theory Lab. Sometimes cited with the subtitle 'Constellating Cultural Rhetorics Practices.' enculturation states the journal is published under a CC Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike license (badge links to 3.0). Long, but sections work as excerpts; the anchor text for a Cultural Rhetorics FYC track.

title: Introduction to the Special Issue: Entering the Cultural Rhetorics Conversations
parent_title: enculturation: a journal of rhetoric, writing, and culture, no. 21
summary: Introduces enculturation's cultural rhetorics special issue drawn from the 2014 Cultural Rhetorics Conference and explains what distinguishes a cultural rhetorics approach, including decolonial delinking and attention to power in comparative work.
notes: Published April 20, 2016. Journal-wide CC BY-NC-SA license statement appears on the page.

title: Welcome to constellations: a kind of storied introduction
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 1
summary: The founding editors introduce the journal and its first issue through two short stories about building a cultural rhetorics publishing space in relation with others.
notes: Site-wide license page: constellations is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (constell8cr.com/creative-commons-license/). Post dated Nov 16, 2018; Powell's section dated May 2018, Hidalgo's April 2019.

title: Rasquache Rhetorics: a cultural rhetorics sensibility
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 1
summary: Develops 'rasquache' (the Chicanx aesthetic of making do with what's at hand) as a rhetorical sensibility, reading lowrider culture and Alma López's controversial 'Our Lady' artwork.
notes: Image-rich webtext; good model for analyzing everyday cultural artifacts.

title: Beyoncé's Performance of Identification as a Diamond: Reclaiming Bodies and Voices in "Formation"
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 1
summary: Reads Beyoncé's 'Formation' video as a performance of identification that reclaims Black women's bodies and voices.
notes: Accessible pop-culture analysis; pairs well with a music video rhetorical analysis assignment.

title: The University of Utah "Utes:" Towards Increased Rhetorical Sovereignty
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 2
summary: Analyzes how University of Utah athletics media guides build a 'Ute' brand through the nickname, logo, and mascot, and argues for greater rhetorical sovereignty for the Ute Tribe.
notes: Written by an undergraduate researcher on the Utes Nickname Project; strong model text for FYC students.

title: The Historical Work of Cultural Rhetorics: Constellating Indigenous, Deaf, and English-Only Literacies
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 2
summary: Connects students' use of Plains Sign Talk at the Carlisle Indian Industrial School to the parallel history of Deaf education and to English-only policy, arguing for historicizing writing curricula.

title: A Settler Archive: A Site for a Decolonial Praxis Project
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 2
summary: Treats a settler archive as a site for decolonial research practice.

title: Countering Racial Enthymemes: What We Can Learn About Race from Donald J. Trump
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 3
summary: Uses examples from Trump's speeches, interviews, and tweets to show how enthymemes can carry racial assumptions, and asks how readers can recognize and counter them.
notes: Links Aristotle's enthymeme to contemporary race talk; useful bridge between classical and cultural rhetorics units.

title: Commemorating Sexism: Suffragist Suppression, Partial Memory, and the Women's Titanic Memorial
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 3
summary: Reads the Women's Titanic Memorial in Washington, DC as an anti-suffrage monument that honors men's sacrifice, and imagines counter-memorial practices.
notes: Title taken from the URL slug and Constellations issue listing; the page title tag reads 'The Sexist Rhetoric of the Women's Titanic Memorial Statue.' Good model for a memorial-analysis assignment.

title: Constellating Stories and Counterstories: Cultural Rhetorics Scholarship Principles
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 4
summary: First of three recorded editor conversations defining cultural rhetorics; participants share origin stories and describe what story, counterstory, and citation practice mean in cultural rhetorics scholarship.
notes: Conversation genre with multiple constellations editors (including Ana Milena Ribero); moderator named in the series as Kimberly Wieser. Published May 11, 2021. Conversational format is very readable for undergraduates.

title: Ethically Working Within Communities: Cultural Rhetorics Methodologies Principles
authors: Arellano, Sonia C.; Hsu, Jo; McGee, Lexi; Brentnell, Lauren
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 4
summary: Editors discuss principles for cultural rhetorics research, including 'staying close to home,' building networks of trust and care, and giving back to communities.
notes: Published June 7, 2021; moderated by Sonia C. Arellano. Participant list taken from speakers named on the page; there may be others.

title: Community, Voice, Identity: The Principles of Cultural Rhetorics Pedagogies
authors: Ribero, Ana Milena; Riley Mukavetz, Andrea; Wieser, Kimberly; Erby, Brandon M.
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 4
summary: Teachers describe cultural rhetorics pedagogies built around story, community, relationships, and land, with concrete examples such as podcasting assignments and community-based courses.
notes: Published July 5, 2021; moderated by Ana Milena Ribero. Directly useful for designing a Cultural Rhetorics FYC track.

title: Listening to Stories: Practicing Cultural Rhetorics Pedagogy
parent_title: constellations Pedagogy Blog
summary: A virtual roundtable on cultural rhetorics pedagogy organized around story, community, relationships, and land.
notes: Roundtable hosted by Margaret Price (then Pedagogy Blog editor); listed on the site as 'Christina V. Cedillo et al.' Other participants not recorded here. Dated May 1, 2018.

title: Wanaragua: Resistance, Recognition and Resilience Among The Garinagu
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 4
summary: Examines Wanaragua, a Garifuna dance tradition, as embodied rhetoric of resistance, recognition, and resilience.
notes: Title from the page's title tag; the issue listing gives a longer form beginning 'Wanaragua: An Embodied Performance of Resistance, Recognition and Resilience...'. Published Nov 3, 2021.

title: My Name is /KLA-ris/: The Bordered Name of an American Latina
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 6
summary: An autoethnographic essay on how the pronunciation of the author's name marks borders of language, culture, and Latina identity in the United States.
notes: Published Aug 15, 2023. Short, personal, and a strong model for a literacy narrative or name essay in FYC.

title: Language as a Moving Anchor: Jhumpa Lahiri's Whereabouts, Asian/American Rhetorics & the Politics of "Linguistic Migration"
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 5
summary: Reads Jhumpa Lahiri's choice to write in Italian as 'linguistic migration' and considers what it means for Asian/American rhetorics and language politics.
notes: Published Dec 6, 2022.

title: Rapsody's Rhetorical Interventions: Black Women & the Hip-Hop Imaginary
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 6
summary: Analyzes rapper Rapsody's 2019 album 'Eve' as an intervention in hip-hop's gendered imaginary that represents Black women as multidimensional.
notes: Published Apr 3, 2024.

title: Transnational Cultural Rhetorics: Introduction to Special Issue 7 of constellations
authors: Cedillo, Christina; Wieser-Weryackwe, Kimberly Gail; Ribero, Ana Milena
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 7
summary: Introduces a special issue on transnational cultural rhetorics and how cultural rhetorics travels across national borders.
notes: Published Nov 18, 2024.

title: Constellating Jewish Rhetorics: A Call for New Directions from an Iraqi Jew
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 8
summary: Calls for new directions in Jewish rhetorics that account for Iraqi and other Mizrahi Jewish histories.
notes: Published Feb 10, 2026.

title: 4C4Equality: Writing Networks for Social Justice
parent_title: constellations: a cultural rhetorics publishing space, Issue 1
summary: A zine-style webtext of interviews, scene reports, and columns from the 4C4Equality network on grassroots organizing and activist writing.
notes: Listed in Issue 1 but dated Jan 23, 2021 on the site. 4C4Equality also publishes Spark: A 4C4Equality Journal.

title: "If you don't want us there, you don't get us": A Statement on Indigenous Visibility and Reconciliation
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 9, no. 2
summary: Two Ojibwe and Choctaw scholars from the CCCC American Indian Caucus respond to repeated requests to guide settlers in making amends, explaining Indigenous sovereignty, NDN time, and what making Indigenous space requires.
notes: Posted March 1, 2022 in the NCTE/CCCC Cross-Caucus special issue. License from Present Tense submissions page: journal uses CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 United States.

title: Backchannel Pedagogies: Unsettling Racial Teaching Moments and White Futurity
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 9, no. 2
summary: Examines how universities repackage racist incidents as 'teaching moments' and how that move reflects a white temporality that delays racial justice.
notes: Posted March 1, 2022.

title: Volume 9.2: NCTE/CCCC Cross-Caucus Present Tense "Diversity is not an End Game: BIPOC Futures in the Academy"
authors: Cedillo, Christina V.; Ore, Ersula J.; Wieser, Kimberly Gail
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 9, no. 2
summary: Introduction to a special issue in which BIPOC scholars of rhetoric and composition critique university diversity work as an 'end game' and describe strategies for surviving and resisting it.
notes: Posted March 1, 2022.

title: Against Hillbilly Hot Takes: Humanizing Rural Appalachia through Nuanced Rhetorical Frames
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 9, no. 3
summary: Shows how media 'hot takes' flatten rural Appalachia into a monolith and proposes more nuanced rhetorical frames that account for Black, Indigenous, and working-class Appalachians.
notes: Posted December 12, 2022. Short and accessible.

title: Bad Ideas About Writing
authors: Ball, Cheryl E.; Loewe, Drew M.
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
topics: students' right to their own language
summary: An edited collection of 62 short essays by writing scholars, each debunking a common bad idea about writing, writers, grammar, genres, assessment, technology, or writing teachers.
notes: Editors (Ball and Loewe). LICENSE CONFLICT: the PDF copyright page says CC BY 4.0 and 'first published in 2017'; the WVU landing page says CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Recorded the book's own copyright-page license; treat as CC BY-NC-ND to be safe until resolved. Other agents may also list this book; chapter records here cover the rhetoric and language-diversity essays.

title: Rhetoric is Synonymous with Empty Speech
parent_title: Bad Ideas About Writing
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
summary: Argues against the popular use of 'rhetoric' to mean empty or deceptive talk and explains rhetoric as the study and practice of persuasion in public life.
notes: See book record for license conflict. Short; a good first-day reading for a rhetoric unit.

title: There is One Correct Way of Writing and Speaking
parent_title: Bad Ideas About Writing
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
topics: students' right to their own language
summary: Challenges the belief that a single 'correct' English exists and shows how that belief privileges some speakers while penalizing others.
notes: See book record for license conflict.

title: African American Language is not Good English
parent_title: Bad Ideas About Writing
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
summary: Explains African American Language as a rule-governed language variety and argues against treating it as 'bad English' in schools.
notes: See book record for license conflict. Pairs with the CCCC Black Linguistic Justice statement.

title: Official American English is Best
parent_title: Bad Ideas About Writing
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
summary: Critiques English-only and 'official English' arguments and makes the case for multilingualism in the United States.
notes: See book record for license conflict.

title: Leave Yourself Out of Your Writing
parent_title: Bad Ideas About Writing
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
summary: Argues that writers should bring their identities and experiences into their writing rather than hiding behind an impersonal voice.
notes: Followed in the book by a response essay by Kimberly N. Parker. See book record for license conflict.

title: Students Should Learn About the Logical Fallacies
parent_title: Bad Ideas About Writing
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
summary: Questions the usefulness of teaching lists of logical fallacies and suggests more rhetorical ways to evaluate arguments.
notes: See book record for license conflict.

title: Logos is Synonymous with Logic
parent_title: Bad Ideas About Writing
publisher_platform: West Virginia University Libraries, Digital Publishing Institute
summary: Explains why logos in classical rhetoric means more than formal logic and how equating the two distorts the rhetorical appeals.
notes: See book record for license conflict.

title: President Woodrow Wilson's 14 Points (Address to Congress, January 8, 1918)
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
license: Public Domain (US federal government work; published 1918)
summary: Wilson's address to Congress setting out a 14-point program for peace after World War I, including the proposal that became the League of Nations.
notes: Public domain as a presidential address (federal work) and by date. NARA page includes context essay and transcript. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Annual Message to Congress (The Four Freedoms Speech), January 6, 1941
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
summary: FDR's 1941 State of the Union, which made the case for aiding Europe's democracies and closed by naming four essential freedoms: of speech, of worship, from want, and from fear.
notes: Official presidential address; US government work, not subject to copyright. Pairs with Norman Rockwell's Four Freedoms paintings for visual rhetoric. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Joint Address to Congress Leading to a Declaration of War Against Japan (December 8, 1941)
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
summary: The 'date which will live in infamy' address asking Congress to declare war after the attack on Pearl Harbor.
notes: Official presidential address; US government work. NARA also holds the annotated draft, useful for revision-as-rhetoric lessons. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Farewell Address (January 17, 1961)
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
summary: Eisenhower's televised farewell, best known for warning against the 'unwarranted influence' of the military-industrial complex.
notes: Official presidential address; US government work. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Inaugural Address (January 20, 1961)
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
summary: Kennedy's inaugural address ('ask not what your country can do for you'), a standard text for studying antithesis, chiasmus, and other stylistic figures.
notes: Official presidential address; US government work. NARA page reproduces Kennedy's draft. JFK Library also hosts the text and video (jfklibrary.org). License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Special Message to the Congress: The American Promise ("We Shall Overcome" speech), March 15, 1965
summary: Johnson's televised address to Congress a week after Bloody Sunday in Selma, urging passage of the Voting Rights Act and adopting the movement's own words: 'And we shall overcome.'
notes: Official presidential address; US government work. LBJ Library transcript cites The American Presidency Project; Miller Center hosts the text with video. Pair with Obama's 2015 Selma remarks. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Address to the Nation on the Explosion of the Space Shuttle Challenger (January 28, 1986)
summary: Reagan's brief televised eulogy after the Challenger disaster, a model of epideictic (ceremonial) speech that ends by quoting John Gillespie Magee's poem 'High Flight.'
notes: Official presidential address; US government work. The quoted lines from 'High Flight' are a separate work. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Remarks by the President at the 50th Anniversary of the Selma to Montgomery Marches (March 7, 2015)
summary: Obama's speech at the Edmund Pettus Bridge commemorating Bloody Sunday, which places Selma in a long American tradition of protest and argues that the work of voting rights is unfinished.
notes: Official remarks by a sitting president; US government work. (Obama's campaign speeches, such as 'A More Perfect Union,' are NOT federal works and are not included.) License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: The Declaration of Independence
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
summary: The 1776 declaration drafted by Jefferson, a foundational American argument whose form was later borrowed by the Seneca Falls Declaration of Sentiments and many protest documents.
notes: NARA transcription of the Stone engraving at landing_url; Project Gutenberg ebook #1 (html_url) is marked 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Chinese Exclusion Act (An act to execute certain treaty stipulations relating to Chinese), 1882
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
summary: The 1882 law banning Chinese laborers from immigrating to the United States and barring Chinese residents from naturalization; the first major US law restricting immigration by ethnicity.
notes: Use as context for Wong Chin Foo's 'Why Am I a Heathen?' (1887) and other Chinese American responses. NARA page includes a transcript and history through the 1943 repeal and 2011-2012 congressional resolutions. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: President Andrew Jackson's Message to Congress 'On Indian Removal' (1830)
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
license: Public Domain (US federal government work; published 1830)
summary: Jackson's December 1830 message defending the Indian Removal Act, a key text of settler-colonial rhetoric.
notes: Read alongside Native responses such as William Apess and Red Jacket, and Hallsby's chapter on settler-colonial rhetorics. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Executive Order 9066 (1942)
parent_title: National Archives Milestone Documents
summary: The February 1942 order that authorized the forced removal and incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II.
notes: NARA page titled 'Executive Order 9066: Resulting in Japanese-American Incarceration (1942).' Useful for studying euphemism and bureaucratic language. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo (February 2, 1848)
parent_title: The Avalon Project
publisher_platform: Avalon Project, Lillian Goldman Law Library, Yale Law School
summary: The treaty ending the U.S.-Mexican War, ceding roughly half of Mexico's territory to the United States and setting terms for Mexicans who remained.
notes: Treaty text is public domain; Avalon's site design is its own. Articles VIII and IX (on property and citizenship) are the usual focus in Chicanx rhetorics units. License basis: no license statement on the page; public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government (17 U.S.C. 105) or by publication date.

title: Gettysburg Address (November 19, 1863)
summary: Lincoln's 272-word dedication of the Soldiers' National Cemetery, the classic example of epideictic brevity in American oratory.
notes: Gutenberg ebook #4 marked 'Public domain in the USA.' Library of Congress exhibit presents the Nicolay and Hay manuscript drafts, useful for comparing versions.

title: Second Inaugural Address (March 4, 1865)
summary: Lincoln's short address near the end of the Civil War that frames the war as judgment for slavery and closes 'with malice toward none, with charity for all.'
notes: Gutenberg ebook #8.

title: Give Me Liberty or Give Me Death
summary: Henry's 1775 speech to the Virginia Convention urging armed resistance to Britain.
notes: The familiar text was reconstructed decades later (commonly attributed to William Wirt's 1817 biography); a good case for discussing how speeches are remembered and rewritten.

title: Speech on Conciliation with America
summary: Burke's long parliamentary speech arguing for reconciliation with the American colonies, long used in schools as a model of deliberative oratory.
notes: Gutenberg ebook #5655.

title: Rhetoric (trans. W. Rhys Roberts)
license: Public Domain (US; Roberts translation first published 1924)
summary: Aristotle's three-book treatise defining rhetoric as the faculty of observing the available means of persuasion, with the three proofs, the three genres of oratory, the topics, emotions, style, and arrangement.
notes: MIT archive page confirms 'Translated by W. Rhys Roberts' but carries no PD statement; the 1924 Oxford translation is public domain in the US by date. Alternative PD translation: J. H. Freese (Loeb, 1926) on Perseus (digital text CC BY-SA 3.0 US) at http://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus:text:1999.01.0060 and on Wikisource (marked public domain) at https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Rhetoric_(Freese). Book I.1-3 and II.1 work well as excerpts.

title: Gorgias (trans. Benjamin Jowett)
summary: Socrates questions the famous orator Gorgias and his followers about what rhetoric is, arguing it is a knack for flattery rather than a true art.
notes: Gutenberg page: 'Public domain in the USA.' Translator Benjamin Jowett (1817-1893). Pair with Gorgias's own 'Encomium of Helen' when an open translation is available.

title: Phaedrus (trans. Benjamin Jowett)
summary: A dialogue on love and rhetoric in which Socrates sketches a 'true' rhetoric adapted to different kinds of souls and tells the myth of Theuth on writing and memory.
notes: Gutenberg page: 'Public domain in the USA.' The closing section on writing is a standard reading for digital and multimodal rhetoric units.

title: Apology (trans. Benjamin Jowett)
summary: Socrates' defense speech at his trial, in which he disclaims rhetorical skill while delivering one of antiquity's most influential speeches.
notes: Gutenberg page: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Against the Sophists (trans. George Norlin)
parent_title: Isocrates with an English Translation (Loeb)
license: Public Domain (US; Norlin's Loeb translation first published 1928-1929)
summary: Isocrates' short attack on rival teachers who promise to make anyone eloquent, and his own account of what rhetorical education can and cannot do.
notes: Perseus credits George Norlin and cites a 1980 Harvard reprint; Norlin translated Loeb vols. 1-2 (first published 1928-1929), which are PD in the US by date. No license statement appeared on the Perseus page fetched. Very short (about two pages).

title: Antidosis (trans. George Norlin)
parent_title: Isocrates with an English Translation (Loeb)
license: Public Domain (US; Norlin's Loeb translation first published 1928-1929)
summary: Isocrates' fictional courtroom defense of his life and teaching, including his claim that speech (logos) is what makes civic life possible.
notes: Perseus credits George Norlin. The 'hymn to logos' section (around sections 253-257) is a common excerpt.

title: Institutio Oratoria (trans. H. E. Butler)
summary: Quintilian's twelve-book program for educating an orator from childhood, ending with the ideal of the 'good man skilled in speaking.'
notes: LacusCurtius states the Butler translation (Loeb, 1920-1922) 'is in the public domain'; pages with one asterisk in the URL are PD. Book XII, ch. 1 ('good man skilled in speaking') is at https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Quintilian/Institutio_Oratoria/12A*.html.

title: Cicero's Brutus or History of Famous Orators; also His Orator, or Accomplished Speaker (trans. E. Jones)
summary: Two of Cicero's late rhetorical works: Brutus, a history of Roman oratory, and Orator, his portrait of the ideal speaker who commands the plain, middle, and grand styles.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' De Oratore itself was not found in a verified PD English edition this session.

title: On the Sublime (trans. H. L. Havell)
license: Public Domain (US; Havell translation, translator d. 1913)
summary: The ancient treatise on the sources of elevated, transporting language in oratory and literature.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: The Olynthiacs and the Philippics of Demosthenes (trans. Charles Rann Kennedy)
summary: Demosthenes' speeches urging Athenians to resist Philip of Macedon, the model for later 'philippics.'
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' A second PD translation (A. W. Pickard-Cambridge, Public Orations vol. 1) is Gutenberg #9060.

title: The Orations of Lysias
summary: Courtroom speeches by the Athenian speechwriter Lysias, known for plain style and character-building (ethopoeia).
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Translator not listed in Gutenberg metadata. 'On the Murder of Eratosthenes' is the usual classroom choice.

title: Pericles' Funeral Oration (History of the Peloponnesian War, Book 2; trans. Richard Crawley)
parent_title: The History of the Peloponnesian War
summary: Thucydides' version of Pericles' speech honoring Athens' war dead, a foundational epideictic text often paired with the Gettysburg Address.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' The oration is in Book 2 (chapters 35-46); link points to the full History.

title: A Serious Proposal to the Ladies, for the Advancement of Their True and Greatest Interest (In Two Parts)
summary: Astell's proposal for women's education; Part II includes her own rhetoric and logic advice for women writers and speakers.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Part I appeared in 1694 and Part II in 1697 (standard dates; not shown on the Gutenberg page).

title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
summary: Wollstonecraft's argument that women's apparent inferiority comes from lack of education, and her call for rational education for women.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' The Introduction and Chapter 2 work as excerpts.

title: A Modest Proposal
summary: Swift's satirical proposal that the Irish poor sell their children as food, the standard text for teaching irony, persona, and satire.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Essays of Michel de Montaigne (trans. Charles Cotton, ed. William Carew Hazlitt)
authors: Montaigne, Michel de; Cotton, Charles (translator); Hazlitt, William Carew (editor)
license: Public Domain (US; Cotton translation 17th century, Hazlitt edition 19th century)
summary: The complete essays that gave the genre its name, including 'Of Cannibals' and 'Of the Education of Children.'
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' 'Of Cannibals' is a useful early text on cultural relativism and colonial encounter.

title: Common Sense
summary: Paine's 1776 pamphlet arguing in plain language for American independence.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: The Federalist Papers
authors: Hamilton, Alexander; Madison, James; Jay, John
summary: The 85 newspaper essays arguing for ratification of the U.S. Constitution; No. 10 on faction is the usual excerpt.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: On the Duty of Civil Disobedience
summary: Thoreau's essay, first published in 1849 as 'Resistance to Civil Government,' arguing that individuals must refuse to support unjust government, written after his night in jail for refusing a tax that supported slavery and war.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Narrative of the Life of Frederick Douglass, an American Slave
summary: Douglass's 1845 slave narrative; Chapters 6-7, on learning to read and The Columbian Orator, are a classic literacy narrative.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Why is the Negro Lynched?
summary: Douglass's late essay refuting the justifications offered for lynching, written alongside Ida B. Wells's anti-lynching campaign.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Year is the commonly cited 1894/1895 publication; not confirmed on the Gutenberg page.

title: Walker's Appeal, with a Brief Sketch of His Life; And Also Garnet's Address to the Slaves of the United States of America
summary: Walker's militant 1829 Appeal to the Coloured Citizens of the World and Garnet's 1843 'Address to the Slaves' calling for resistance, printed together by Garnet.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Letters on the Equality of the Sexes, and the Condition of Woman
summary: Sarah Grimké's letters defending women's right to speak publicly against slavery, built on close rereading of scripture.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Original publication Boston: Isaac Knapp, 1838.

title: The Narrative of Sojourner Truth
summary: Sojourner Truth's life story as dictated to Olive Gilbert, raising questions about voice and mediated authorship.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases
summary: Wells's 1892 pamphlet exposing the false rape charges used to justify lynching, using white newspapers' own reports as evidence.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Strong model of evidence-based protest writing.

title: The Red Record: Tabulated Statistics and Alleged Causes of Lynching in the United States
summary: Wells's statistical study of lynching in the United States, compiled largely from white-owned newspaper reports.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Useful for data-driven argument and visual rhetoric of statistics.

title: A Voice from the South, By a Black Woman of the South
summary: Cooper's 1892 essays and speeches on Black women's education and voice, including 'Womanhood a Vital Element in the Regeneration and Progress of a Race.'
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: The Souls of Black Folk
summary: Du Bois's 1903 essays introducing 'double consciousness' and 'the color line'; Chapter 3 answers Booker T. Washington's Atlanta address.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Up from Slavery: An Autobiography (includes the Atlanta Exposition Address)
summary: Washington's autobiography, which reprints and recounts his 1895 Atlanta Exposition address (the 'Atlanta Compromise').
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' A standalone text of the address is on Wikisource (see separate record).

title: Darkwater: Voices from Within the Veil
summary: Du Bois's 1920 collection of essays and poems, including 'The Souls of White Folk' and 'The Damnation of Women.'
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: How It Feels to Be Colored Me
summary: Hurston's short 1928 personal essay on race, identity, and refusing to be 'tragically colored.'
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Entered US public domain in 2024. Short enough for a single class session.

title: Fire!! A Quarterly Devoted to the Younger Negro Artists, Volume 1, Number 1
summary: The single 1926 issue of the Harlem Renaissance little magazine Fire!!, a manifesto-like gathering of fiction, poetry, drama, and art by younger Black writers.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Edited by Wallace Thurman per standard histories; Gutenberg contents credit Aaron Douglas for art decorations. Check the file for the full contributor list before citing individual authors.

title: Women and Economics: A Study of the Economic Relation Between Men and Women as a Factor in Social Evolution
summary: Gilman's 1898 argument that women's economic dependence on men distorts both sexes and society.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Indian Nullification of the Unconstitutional Laws of Massachusetts Relative to the Marshpee Tribe; Or, the Pretended Riot Explained
summary: The Pequot minister William Apess's documentary account and defense of the Mashpee Wampanoag's 1833 assertion of self-government.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Apess's 'An Indian's Looking-Glass for the White Man' and 'Eulogy on King Philip' were not found in a verified free edition this session.

title: American Indian Stories
summary: Zitkala-Ša's autobiographical essays on her Yankton Dakota childhood and boarding-school education, with stories and the essay 'America's Indian Problem.'
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' The boarding-school essays (originally in The Atlantic, 1900) are short and widely taught; 'Why I Am a Pagan' appears here as 'The Great Spirit.'

title: The Soul of the Indian: An Interpretation
summary: Eastman's 1911 account of Dakota spiritual life written for non-Native readers, a case study in addressing a skeptical audience.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Mrs. Spring Fragrance
summary: Stories of Chinese American life by one of the first writers of Chinese descent published in North America; 'In the Land of the Free' depicts immigration enforcement.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Fiction; her essay 'Leaves from the Mental Portfolio of an Eurasian' (1909) is listed on Wikisource but not yet transcribed.

title: My Life in China and America
summary: Memoir by the first Chinese graduate of an American college (Yale, 1854), covering his education and the Chinese Educational Mission.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: The Squatter and the Don: A Novel Descriptive of Contemporary Occurrences in California
summary: The first English-language novel published by a Mexican American woman, protesting the dispossession of Californio landowners after 1848.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Pair with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo.

title: The Intermediate Sex: A Study of Some Transitional Types of Men and Women
summary: Carpenter's 1908 defense of same-sex love and gender variance, an early public argument for gay acceptance.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Uses period terminology; best as historical context for queer rhetorics.

title: Optimism: An Essay
summary: Keller's early essay on optimism, useful for discussing how disabled writers were expected to perform inspiration for nondisabled audiences.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Keller's later socialist writings ('Out of the Dark,' 1913) are listed on Wikisource but not transcribed.

title: Youth and Life
summary: Bourne's 1913 essay collection on youth and modern life, closing with 'A Philosophy of Handicap,' an early first-person essay on disability.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Original publication Houghton Mifflin, 1913. Contents end with 'A Philosophy of Handicap,' Bourne's essay on living with disability.

title: Anarchism and Other Essays
summary: Goldman's 1910 essays on anarchism, patriotism, women's suffrage, and 'The Traffic in Women,' many first delivered as lectures.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: The Common Reader (First Series)
summary: Woolf's 1925 essays on reading and writing, including 'Modern Fiction' and 'The Patron and the Crocus' (on writing for an audience).
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Europe and Elsewhere (includes 'Corn-pone Opinions')
summary: A posthumous 1923 collection of Twain's essays and sketches, including 'Corn-pone Opinions' on how people adopt the opinions of their group.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA'; original publication Harper and Brothers, 1923. The volume is also usually cited for 'The United States of Lyncherdom' and 'The War Prayer'; confirm in the Gutenberg file.

title: Fenimore Cooper's Literary Offences
summary: Twain's comic takedown of James Fenimore Cooper's prose, listing 'rules' of good writing that Cooper breaks.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Useful for style and evaluative argument.

title: What to the Slave Is the Fourth of July? (Oration Delivered in Corinthian Hall, Rochester, July 5, 1852)
summary: Douglass's 1852 address to the Rochester Ladies' Anti-Slavery Society, which turns the Independence Day oration against its audience: 'This Fourth of July is yours, not mine.'
notes: Wikisource transcription is proofread against a scan of the 1852 pamphlet and carries a public domain tag. An extract also appears in the appendix of My Bondage and My Freedom (Project Gutenberg #202, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/202/pg202-images.html).

title: Oration in Memory of Abraham Lincoln (1876)
summary: Douglass's speech at the unveiling of the Freedmen's Memorial in Washington, offering a frank, double-edged assessment of Lincoln before a mixed audience.
notes: Wikisource page carries a public domain tag. Good for public memory and monument units.

title: Women's Rights Convention Speech, Akron, 1851 (Anti-Slavery Bugle version) and 'Ain't I a Woman?' (Gage 1863 version)
license: Public Domain (US; 1851 and 1863 publications; NPS page is a federal work)
summary: Sojourner Truth's 1851 Akron speech in two versions: the report printed weeks later in the Anti-Slavery Bugle and Frances Gage's 1863 recollection that introduced the refrain 'Ain't I a woman?'
notes: Both Wikisource pages carry public domain tags; Gage version at https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/Ain%27t_I_a_Woman%3F. The NPS article prints the Gage text and explains the controversy over versions, which makes a strong lesson on how speeches are mediated and remembered.

title: Declaration of Sentiments (Seneca Falls, 1848)
publisher_platform: U.S. National Park Service (Women's Rights National Historical Park); Wikisource
summary: The Seneca Falls convention's declaration, modeled line by line on the Declaration of Independence, listing grievances against men's 'absolute tyranny' over women.
notes: Wikisource copy carries a public domain tag. Ideal for imitation and genre-borrowing lessons alongside the Declaration of Independence.

title: Solitude of Self (1892)
summary: Stanton's 1892 address to the House Judiciary Committee grounding women's rights in each person's ultimate solitude and self-sovereignty.
notes: Wikisource page carries a public domain tag.

title: On Women's Rights to Vote (1873)
summary: Anthony's short 1873 speech, given after her arrest for voting, arguing that women are 'persons' and citizens entitled to vote under the Constitution.
notes: Wikisource page title is 'On Women's Rights to Vote' and carries a public domain tag. Wikisource also hosts her speech after conviction (1873).

title: Appeal to the Christian Women of the South (1836)
summary: Grimké's 1836 pamphlet urging Southern white women to oppose slavery through reading, prayer, speech, and action, which was burned in South Carolina.
notes: No PD tag captured in this session's check; public domain by 1836 publication date.

title: Atlanta Exposition Address ('Atlanta Compromise'), 1895
summary: Washington's speech to a largely white audience at the Cotton States Exposition, accepting segregation in exchange for economic opportunity ('Cast down your bucket where you are').
notes: Wikisource page carries a public domain tag and links an audio recording. Pair with Du Bois, Souls of Black Folk, ch. 3.

title: Freedom or Death (1913 speech in the United States)
summary: Pankhurst's 1913 speech in the United States defending the militant tactics of British suffragettes to an American audience.
notes: Wikisource public domain tag (author d. 1928).

title: Slavery in Massachusetts (1854)
parent_title: A Yankee in Canada, with Anti-Slavery and Reform Papers (1866)
summary: Thoreau's July 4, 1854 address at Framingham, delivered after the return of fugitive Anthony Burns, attacking Massachusetts's complicity in slavery.
notes: Wikisource public domain tag. 'A Plea for Captain John Brown' (1859) is in the same Wikisource volume.

title: The American Scholar (Phi Beta Kappa Address, 1837)
summary: Emerson's address to Harvard's Phi Beta Kappa Society calling for an American intellectual independence grounded in nature, books, and action.
notes: Wikisource public domain tag. Also in Emerson's Miscellanies, Project Gutenberg #71683.

title: Mr. Bennett and Mrs. Brown (1924)
summary: Woolf's essay on character and the break between Edwardian and Georgian writers, built around an imagined fellow train passenger.
notes: Wikisource public domain tag; PD in US by 1924 publication date.

title: A Room of One's Own (1929)
license: Public Domain (US, published 1929; entered US public domain January 1, 2025)
summary: Woolf's essay, developed from 1928 lectures at Cambridge women's colleges, arguing that a woman needs money and a room of her own to write, with the story of 'Judith Shakespeare.'
notes: Wikisource lists the work (September 1929); PD tag not captured in this session's check. Public domain in the US by date (1929 works entered the US public domain in 2025); may still be under copyright in other countries.

title: Red Jacket on the Religion of the White Man and the Red (1805)
summary: The Seneca orator Red Jacket's reply to a missionary seeking to convert the Haudenosaunee, turning Christian arguments back on their speaker.
notes: Wikisource public domain tag. As with most recorded Native oratory, the English text passed through interpreters and editors; discuss translation and transcription as part of the reading. An 1830s account of Red Jacket and his speeches (Hubbard) is Gutenberg #7339.

title: Tecumseh's Speech, of August 11, 1810, to Governor William Harrison
license: Public Domain (US; 1810 speech in a pre-1931 printed version)
summary: Tecumseh's speech at Vincennes rejecting land cessions made by individual chiefs and asserting that the land belongs to all Native nations in common.
notes: Wikisource public domain tag (the template notes a contributor who died in 1943, so this is a later printed version). Authenticity and translation of Tecumseh speeches vary by source; teach with that caveat. Wikisource also has his speech to the Osages.

title: Life Among the Piutes
publisher_platform: A Celebration of Women Writers (University of Pennsylvania Digital Library)
summary: The first published autobiography by a Native American woman, documenting Northern Paiute history and the injustices of the reservation system as a sustained argument to white readers.
notes: Text page reproduces the 1883 copyright line of Sarah Winnemucca Hopkins (long expired). The Celebration of Women Writers site has its own site copyright notice for its edition and markup; check its terms before redistributing. The page includes an unnamed editor's preface (the 1883 edition is usually credited to editor Mary Peabody Mann; not confirmed this session). Peabody's 1886 pamphlet on Winnemucca's proposals is Gutenberg #57526.

title: Why Am I a Heathen? (The North American Review, vol. 145, 1887)
parent_title: The North American Review, vol. 145, no. 369
summary: Chinese American journalist Wong Chin Foo's 1887 essay explaining why he rejects Christianity, turning the label 'heathen' against American hypocrisy in the era of Chinese exclusion.
notes: PD tag not captured in this session's check; public domain by 1887 publication date. Pair with the Chinese Exclusion Act (1882).

title: Nuestra América (1891)
summary: Martí's 1891 essay calling on Latin American nations to build governments from their own Indigenous and mestizo realities rather than imported European and U.S. models.
notes: Spanish original only; this session found no verified public-domain English translation, so pair with a student or instructor translation activity. Wikisource page carries a 'sin fuente' (no source) notice. Dated on the page 'México, 30 de enero de 1891.'

summary: Uses Black feminist rhetoric to teach Beyoncé's documentary Homecoming in an HBCU writing classroom.

summary: A case study of teaching K-pop in a first-year composition course at an HBCU and what it reveals about the possibilities and difficulties of Afro-Asian solidarity.
notes: JOMR CC BY 4.0.

parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 9, no. 1

title: Abolitionist Podcasting: Amplifying Queer and Trans Activists of Color

parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 10, no. 1 (Composing at the Intersections: Queer, Trans*, Feminist Multimodal Rhetorics)
summary: Analyzes how detransitioned people on TikTok use digital counterstorytelling to resist anti-trans uses of detransition narratives.

summary: A webtext with two reading paths (academic and 'crip resource') on navigating graduate school as a disabled student.

authors: Sanders, Nick; Haywood, Constance; Pouncil, Floyd; Mendoza, Ruby
parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 10, no. 1

notes: JOMR CC BY 4.0. Landing URL taken from the issue table of contents link; issue page is html_url.

parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 5, no. 1

notes: JOMR CC BY 4.0; PDF version linked on page.

title: On 'Crip Doulas,' Invisible Labor, and Surviving Academia while Disabled
parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 5, no. 1
summary: Reflects on the invisible labor of disabled academics and the practice of 'crip doulaship,' disabled people supporting one another.
notes: JOMR CC BY 4.0; PDF version linked on page.

title: Decolonial Directions: Rivers, Relationships, and Realities of Community Engagement on Indigenous Lands
parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 4, no. 1 (Curation: A Multimodal Practice for Socially-Engaged Action)
summary: A digital installation curating two academics' experiences of decolonial community engagement on Indigenous lands in Oklahoma, organized around rivers and relationships.
notes: JOMR CC BY 4.0. Special issue co-curated by Maria Novotny and Ames Hawkins, drawing on the 2016 Cultural Rhetorics Exhibition.

title: Sounding Out a Rhetoric of Resilience: Curating Plena in DiaspoRican Activism
parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 4, no. 1 (Curation: A Multimodal Practice for Socially-Engaged Action)
summary: A creative-critical sound curation of plena, the 'sung newspapers' of Puerto Rico, as a rhetoric of Puerto Rican resilience and diasporic activism.
notes: JOMR CC BY 4.0. Multimodal (audio) piece.

title: Tweet to #SaveWomensSports: Visualizing Anti-Trans Stigma in Athletics
parent_title: The Journal of Multimodal Rhetorics, vol. 8, no. 1
summary: Examines a 2021 beer-brand 'save women's sports' campaign and how the #SaveWomensSports hashtag was taken up to spread anti-trans stigma.
notes: JOMR CC BY 4.0.

title: No Más MAS: Teachers Defining Pedagogies and Themselves in a Post-Ethnic Studies Arizona
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 7, no. 1
summary: Interviews Tucson teachers about how they defined their pedagogies and identities after Arizona banned the Mexican American Studies (MAS) program.
notes: Posted May 5, 2018. Journal-wide license CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US.

title: The Indecorous Objects of Social Transformation
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 7, no. 1
summary: Reads the many unstandardized designs of transgender-inclusive restroom placards as evidence of social change in progress around LGBTQ rights.
notes: Posted May 3, 2018. Short and concrete; good for a visual rhetoric artifact assignment.

title: Horrorism and Ontological Dignity: What Do/not Historical Signs Tell Us?
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 7, no. 1
summary: Analyzes what historical signs say and leave unsaid about the places they mark, and how their rhetorical absences shape the impression visitors take away.
notes: Posted May 4, 2018. Pairs with memorial and public memory assignments.

title: Viewing Sleep Dealer as Teoria Povera in the Trump Era: Rhetorical Coloniality, Reality Television, and Water Dispossession
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 8, no. 1
summary: Reads the Spanish-English science fiction film Sleep Dealer, set behind a sealed U.S.-Mexico border, as theory about rhetorical coloniality and water dispossession.
notes: Posted November 13, 2019.

title: The Crossing as Constitutional Rhetoric: Balsero Art and Identity from Cuban Refugee Camps and Implications for Cuban-American Relations
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 6, no. 1
summary: Examines drawings by children in Cuban refugee camps as constitutive rhetoric that shaped balsero (rafter) identity.
notes: Posted October 5, 2016.

title: Composing Artificial Intelligence: Performing Whiteness and Masculinity
parent_title: Present Tense: A Journal of Rhetoric in Society, vol. 6, no. 1
summary: Argues that cultural representations of artificial intelligence tie intelligence to whiteness and masculinity, and that undoing tech-culture injustice requires disentangling them.
notes: Posted October 6, 2016. Timely for AI units.

title: Public Speaking (Lumen Learning)
summary: A modular introductory public speaking text covering ethical speech, listening, audience analysis and cultural competence, organization, delivery, persuasion (including ethos, logos, pathos and Monroe's Motivated Sequence), online speaking, and workplace speaking.
notes: CC BY 4.0 per LibreTexts page; adapted from courses.lumenlearning.com/wm-publicspeaking. Fully remixable. Ch. 2 Ethical Speech and Ch. 10 Persuasive Speaking are the most rhetoric-centered chapters.

title: Messages that Matter: Public Speaking in the Information Age (3e)
summary: An introductory public speaking text with chapters on communication basics, speech anxiety, audience analysis, framing language, critical listening, visual aids, persuasion theories, and motivating action.
notes: LibreTexts page states 'CC BY' without a version number; license_url assumes 4.0, confirm in front matter.

title: It's About Them: Public Speaking in the 21st Century
authors: Kim, Sara; Marshall, Douglas; Pulliam, June; VanNest, Victoria; Yeargain, James
summary: An audience-centered introductory public speaking text from the Louisiana LOUIS network, with chapters on confidence, audience analysis, listening, ethics, argument, delivery, persuasive, informative, special occasion, and online speaking.
notes: Chapter structure closely tracks Stand Up, Speak Out.

title: Diving into Rhetoric: A Rhetorical View of History, Communication, and Composition
license: CC BY-NC-SA (per search-result summary; not confirmed on page)
summary: An introductory rhetoric text with a brief history of rhetoric from classical Greece and Rome to modern theory, ending with a Rogerian argument assignment.
notes: Book page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetches this session; title, author, and license come from a web search summary only. A 2026 copy exists at pressbooks.pub/divingintorhetoric2026. Verify before use.

title: Cicero on Oratory and Orators, with His Letters to Quintus and Brutus (trans. J. S. Watson; includes De Oratore)
authors: Cicero, Marcus Tullius; Watson, J. S. (translator)
license: Public Domain (US; this printing 1896, translator d. 1884)
summary: John Selby Watson's 19th-century English translation of Cicero's dialogue De Oratore (on the ideal orator and the five canons) together with related letters.
notes: IA record: publication date 1896; copyright evidence note says 'no visible notice of copyright; stated date is 1896.' An 1871 printing (ciceroonoratory00cice_202507) and an 1860 printing (ciceroonoratoryo0000jswa) are also on IA. Scanned book, not clean HTML; Book I and the memory passage in Book II are typical excerpts.

title: Lectures on Rhetoric and Belles Lettres
license: Public Domain (US; first published 1783, this edition 1812)
summary: Blair's enormously influential lectures on taste, style, and eloquence, a foundation of 19th-century rhetoric and composition teaching in Britain and the United States.
notes: IA scan of an 1812 multi-volume edition (this item is one volume; check which). Many other editions on IA, including 1787 and 1813. Scanned book.

title: The Philosophy of Rhetoric
license: Public Domain (US; first published 1776, this edition 1854)
summary: Campbell's Enlightenment rhetoric, which defines eloquence by its effects on the understanding, imagination, passions, and will of an audience.
notes: IA record: publication date 1854; 'no visible notice of copyright.' Scanned book. Book I, ch. 1 (the four ends of speaking) is the usual excerpt.

title: Elements of Rhetoric: Comprising the Substance of the Article in the Encyclopaedia Metropolitana
summary: Whately's 1828 treatise on argumentative composition, known for its account of presumption and burden of proof.
notes: IA metadata: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; 1828 London (John Murray) printing digitized by Google from Harvard.

title: Women's Speaking Justified, Proved and Allowed of by the Scriptures (1666)
publisher_platform: Quaker Heritage Press (transcription); Internet Archive (1666 scan)
summary: The Quaker leader Margaret Fell's scriptural defense of women's right to preach and speak in church, a founding text in the history of women's rhetoric.
notes: Quaker Heritage Press page (readable transcription) was reachable earlier in the session but timed out on a later check; IA hosts a scan of the 1666 printing and a 1667 printing. Full title as commonly given; the IA record title is truncated ('Women's speaking justified ... 1666').

title: Meditations from the Pen of Mrs. Maria W. Stewart (1879 edition; first presented 1832)
summary: An 1879 edition of Maria W. Stewart's meditations, first presented in 1832 to Boston's First African Baptist Church, by one of the earliest African American women political speakers and writers.
notes: IA title: 'Meditations from the pen of Mrs. Maria W. Stewart, (widow of the late James W. Stewart,) now matron of the Freedmen's Hospital, and presented in 1832 to the First African Baptist Church and Society of Boston.' Whether this edition includes her 1832-1833 public lectures was not confirmed; scanned book. Her 'Lecture Delivered at Franklin Hall' (1832) was not found in a verified free edition this session.

title: On Christian Doctrine, Book IV (trans. J. F. Shaw)
authors: Augustine of Hippo; Shaw, James F. (translator)
parent_title: On Christian Doctrine
publisher_platform: New Advent (from Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, 1887); Christian Classics Ethereal Library
license: Public Domain (US; Shaw translation published 1887). New Advent's light revisions and site are copyrighted.
summary: Augustine's book on Christian eloquence, adapting Cicero's three styles and three duties of the orator (to teach, to delight, to move) for preaching.
notes: New Advent page credits James Shaw's translation from NPNF First Series vol. 2 (Christian Literature Publishing, 1887), 'revised and edited for New Advent by Kevin Knight,' with a New Advent copyright notice; link to it but do not copy its text. CCEL hosts the unrevised NPNF text (work page at landing_url; book/chapter pages load dynamically).

title: My Bondage and My Freedom (with appendix of speech extracts)
summary: Douglass's second autobiography (1855), whose appendix reprints extracts from his lectures and orations, including the Rochester July 5, 1852 address.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: The New Freedom: A Call for the Emancipation of the Generous Energies of a People
summary: Wilson's 1912 campaign speeches, edited into book form in 1913, laying out his progressive program.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: Mark Twain's Speeches
summary: A collection of Twain's after-dinner and occasional speeches, useful models of humor, timing, and audience adaptation in ceremonial speaking.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.'

title: The Past and the Present Condition, and the Destiny, of the Colored Race
summary: Garnet's discourse on the history, present condition, and future of people of African descent.
notes: Gutenberg: 'Public domain in the USA.' Year from the work's standard 1848 dating; not shown in the Gutenberg title.
